todays-aba-foundations.title: Today's ABA Foundations: From Compliance to Compassion

questions.explain: Today's ABA starts with safety and rapport. Demands and assessment wait until the learner is happy, relaxed, and engaged — trust first, teaching second.
Any sign of distress or protest is honored immediately. Relent, restore HRE, and repeat — this is how empowerment and trust are built.
Assent is continuous, observable, and revocable — the learner votes with their feet, voice, and affect in every moment.
By enriching contexts, following the learner's lead, never coercing through distress, and making decisions from performance — the process itself avoids re-traumatization.
Freedom to leave is both dignifying and informative — it tells you exactly when your context needs revision.

pfa-interview-informed.title: Practical Functional Assessment: The Interview-Informed Process

questions.explain: The interview centers voices of those who know and love the learner — revealing loves, aversions, and evocative contexts no checklist can capture.
Real life doesn't isolate variables — the IISCA tests the synthesized establishing operation (e.g., denied access + demands + removed attention) together.
Televisibility is an ethical test: if you'd flinch at a family watching, redesign the procedure.
Safety first: enriched return contexts, clear termination criteria, and trained implementers are non-negotiable.
PFA answers 'why' — understanding first — so treatment (SBT) can teach replacement skills under the same motivating conditions.
The FCR must work where it matters — under the real EO — and work every time at first, so the learner trusts their new voice.
The learner's behavior is the compass. Progress, pause, or back up based on what you see now — not at next week's meeting.
Resurgence is information, not defiance. Adjust the challenge to match current capacity and protect trust.
CABs are the payoff: participating in circle time, waiting in line, doing homework — childhood, reclaimed.
SBT aims at lives, not just data paths — skills the learner and family genuinely value, generalized everywhere.
Assent-based practice weaves all four principles together — benefiting others, integrity, compassion/dignity/respect, and cultural responsiveness.
All behavior communicates. Turning away and pushing materials are classic withdrawal signals — honor first, analyze second.
Universal precautions for dignity: assume trauma histories, prioritize safety, rapport, and agency for everyone.
Assent is continuous — document the ongoing conversation, not a one-time signature.

play-first-naturalistic.title: Play First: Naturalistic Teaching for Early Learners

questions.explain: Pairing makes YOU the reinforcer — the child should light up when you arrive, before any demand is ever placed.
Join first, then gently expand. Shared joy opens the door to new play and language.
NET harnesses intrinsic motivation in real contexts — learning sticks because it's meaningful.
Routines are the curriculum — snack, bath, and bedtime beat flashcards every time.

speech-aba-collaboration.title: Speech + ABA Collaboration: Building Total Communicators

questions.explain: No modality hierarchy — the best communication is the communication that works for the learner right now.
Shared, measurable goals with complementary strategies — communication IS behavior.
Decades of research: AAC supports spoken language development while giving learners a voice today.

supervising-with-heart.title: Supervising with Heart: Compassionate Supervision & Mentorship

questions.explain: Timely, specific, behavior-focused feedback with a clear path forward — kindness AND clarity.
Show me, don't tell me — competence is demonstrated with real learners under observation.
Supervisors protect the workforce. Listen first, then adjust systems — starting with your own expectations.

family-partnership-coaching.title: Partnering with Families: Caregiver Coaching That Sticks

questions.explain: Families know their child best. Our job is to add tools to their expertise — not replace it.
Explain briefly, model it, practice together with support, then celebrate — every coaching moment follows the rhythm.
Non-implementation is feedback about OUR plan's fit. Redesign with the family, not against them.
Your capstone tells a story: how safety, listening, and skill-building changed a learner's trajectory.
Today's ABA is profoundly relational. Live practice with coaching builds the judgment no recording can.
